newsitem.title: NIGERIA: Two Nigerian suspects die in prison custody.
newsitem.headline: Two Nigerian suspects die in prison custody.

text.p: Two suspects awaiting trial died from torture in a prison in central Nigeria two weeks ago, the state-owned News Agency of Nigeria (NAN) reported on Thursday.
It said other suspects on remand revealed the deaths to the chief judge of Kwara state Justice Timothy Oyeyipo on Wednesday when he visited the prison in the state capital Ilorin.
They told the judge the deaths were "not unconnected with torture they received from the police before being sent to prison custody", NAN reported.
The judge responded that no one should be subjected to torture by the police.
"Our country still subscribes to the rule of law and only recently the federal government set up a human rights commission which underscores that fact," Oyeyipo said.
Military-ruled Nigeria has been under fire from home and abroad for alleged human rights abuses and lack of democracy.

Last week, two United Nations envoys due to investigate the rights situation cancelled their proposed visit to Nigeria at the last moment when the government refused to allow them access to jails and political detainees.
The government now expects an African human rights team to arrive on Friday for a one-week stay to undertake the same assignment.

Prison authorities and human rights activists have long complained of over-crowding in Nigerian prisons which together hold about 55,000, twice the number they were built for and more than half the total are suspects awaiting trial.
In January, 37 suspects were freed after being held for up to 10 years without charge following the intervention of the human rights group, the Constitutional Rights Project.
